html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. XLSX: Excel workbook file; HTML: hypertext markup language

  • The main features of Claude and what each is for
  • How to choose the lightest feature that fits the task
  • The difference between web search, extended thinking and Research
  • What you can do with files, Projects, Artifacts, Skills and connectors

2The Feature Map

Running case

Cedarbrook's Monday Requests

  • Customer care wants a quick reply draft
  • Finance wants a board-ready analysis of regional returns from a spreadsheet
  • Marketing wants a competitor price scan with sources
  • Operations wants a standing assistant that knows the packing procedures
  • Each request needs a different feature

Feature What it does Use it for
Chat Conversation with Claude Drafting, explaining, brainstorming, quick edits
Web search Looks up live web content; gives citations Simple, current facts needing one or two lookups
Extended thinking Claude reasons through the problem before answering Hard reasoning with no need for recent web data: math, logic, debugging, multi-angle analysis
Research Multi-step investigation across the web and your connected tools; produces a cited report Comprehensive gathering (about five or more lookups, a few minutes)
File upload Reads PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, XLSX and more, plus images Summaries, analysis and Q&A on your documents
Create and edit files Builds Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF files in a sandbox Reports, slide decks, spreadsheets, charts
Artifacts Side-panel content you can edit, reuse and share Documents, slides, dashboards, small tools
Projects A workspace with instructions and knowledge for many chats Recurring work needing the same background (Module 11)
Memory and chat search Remembers context across chats; finds past chats Continuity (Module 8)
Skills Reusable procedures Claude loads when relevant Repeatable tasks with a set method (Module 12)
Connectors Link Claude to apps such as Google Drive, Gmail, Slack Working with your own data and tools (Module 12)
Exam tip

Choose the lightest feature that fits the task. Research for a one-line fact, or plain chat for a competitor report, are both mismatches.

3Search, Thinking and Research

Web search Extended thinking Research
Best for A current fact: news, a price, company info Complex reasoning without needing the web Deep, multi-source investigation
Typical effort One or two tool calls Claude thinks longer before answering Five or more lookups, about 1 to 3 minutes
Output Short answer with citations A reasoned answer A longer report with citations
Sources Web Your prompt and what Claude knows Web plus your connected tools (for example Google Workspace)
Examples "What is the current return window at a rival?" "Optimize this packing schedule", "find the logic error in this formula" "Compare five rivals' pricing and warranty terms and recommend a position"
  • Web search must be available to Claude; on Team and Enterprise plans an owner enables it for the workspace first [Verify live]. On some versions Claude decides when to search; you can always say "search the web" or "do not search".
  • Research is a paid-plan feature [Verify live]; it uses more of your usage limit because it retrieves many sources. On mobile it may search only the web and skip connectors.
  • Research plus thinking: thinking plans the approach and Research carries out the gathering.
  • For all three, verify what you will rely on (Module 4).
Exam tip

Key words: "current fact" points to web search; "reason through" or "complex logic" points to extended thinking; "comprehensive report with sources" points to Research.

4Files, Projects, Artifacts and More

  • File upload. Supported documents include PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX; images include JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP. In a chat: up to 20 files, 500 MB each; PDFs up to 1,000 pages (100 pages or fewer: text and visuals are analyzed; 101 to 1,000: text only). Split very large documents. Non-PDF documents yield text only, so embedded images are not read [Verify live].
  • Create and edit files. With Create and edit files (code execution) on, Claude builds Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF files, writes scripts and makes charts in a private sandbox. Files can be downloaded or saved to Google Drive (about 30 MB). File creation uses more of your usage limit.
  • Artifacts. For substantial, reusable content such as documents, slides, designs and small tools (Module 5).
  • Projects. Standing instructions plus a knowledge base for related chats. Prefer a Project over re-pasting the same background (Module 11).
  • Skills. Folders of instructions loaded only when relevant; ideal for a repeatable method such as "our report format" (Module 12).
  • Connectors. Give Claude access to Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar and other services within your permissions (Module 12).
  • Images. Claude can read images, charts and screenshots. It does not create photos or illustrations like an image generator; it can build diagrams and charts.

[Verify live] Names, plan availability and limits move quickly. The principle holds: match the feature to the need.

5A Feature Chooser

If the request is... Choose
A quick draft or explanation Chat
A single current fact Web search
A hard logic or math problem Extended thinking (and verify)
A cited, multi-source report Research
Questions about your documents File upload (or a Project)
The same background every week Project
A deliverable people will edit or share Artifact or file
The same method every time Skill
Data in Drive or Gmail Connector
Exam tip

Connectors, web search and Research widen what Claude can see and use more of your limit, so turn on only what the task needs.

6Exam Q&A

S1A marketer needs the current published price of one competitor product. Which feature fits best?

  • AWeb search in a normal chat
  • BA Project with 50 files
  • CResearch, to produce a long report
  • DCreate a Skill
Show the answer

Answer: A. A simple current fact needs one or two lookups.

S2A strategist wants a comprehensive, cited comparison of five rivals' pricing, warranty and shipping terms. Which feature fits best?

  • APlain chat with no tools
  • BMemory
  • CResearch
  • DAn image upload
Show the answer

Answer: C. Research handles multi-step, multi-source investigation with a cited report.

S3An analyst must find the logic error in a complicated discount rule that needs no outside data. Which feature helps most?

  • AExtended thinking
  • BWeb search
  • CResearch
  • DA connector
Show the answer

Answer: A. Hard reasoning with no need for current web facts is the use case for extended thinking.

S4A team lead pastes the same 800-word brand-voice guide at the start of every chat. What is the better setup?

  • AKeep pasting it at the start of every new chat as before
  • BAsk Claude to remember it by chance
  • CPut it in a Project's instructions or knowledge
  • DEmail it to Claude
Show the answer

Answer: C. Standing context that is needed again and again belongs in a Project, so every chat starts with the same background without pasting.

S5A user uploads a 1,500-page PDF and sees a "file too large" error. What should they do?

  • ASplit it into smaller sections under the page limit
  • BTurn off Research
  • CChange the model
  • DRetry the same file several times until the error clears
Show the answer

Answer: A. PDFs over 1,000 pages cannot be uploaded; split large documents.

S6Which TWO tasks are best done with Create and edit files? Select TWO.

  • ABuilding an Excel workbook with charts from sales data
  • BProducing a PowerPoint deck from meeting notes
  • CLooking up today's weather
  • DAnswering a yes-or-no question
  • ESearching past chats
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. File creation builds Office and PDF files from your material.

S7A manager asks Claude to paint a realistic photo of a tent in the mountains. What is true?

  • AClaude can generate realistic photos only when Research mode is switched on and a connector is added
  • BClaude generates photos like a dedicated image tool
  • CClaude does not generate photos like an image tool, but it can read images and build diagrams
  • DClaude only works with text
Show the answer

Answer: C. Image generation is not a Claude capability; reading images and building diagrams is.

S8Which request is the poorest match to Research?

  • AA multi-source summary of regulations that affect packaging
  • BA cited competitor landscape for a board paper
  • CA report that combines web findings with Google Drive documents
  • DWhat time does the store down the road close?
Show the answer

Answer: D. A quick lookup does not need a multi-minute investigation.

S9Why might a team limit the use of Research and file creation on busy days?

  • AThey cost the same as a single short message in an ordinary chat
  • BThey consume more of the usage limit than ordinary chat
  • CThey are banned on weekdays so that capacity is kept for other users of the service
  • DThey only work at night
Show the answer

Answer: B. Multi-step tools and file creation use more of your allowance.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Principle Lightest feature that fits
Web search Current facts; one or two lookups; citations
Extended thinking Hard reasoning; no web needed
Research Five or more lookups, about 1 to 3 minutes; cited report; web plus connectors; paid plans
Files Up to 20 per chat, 500 MB each; PDF 1,000 pages max (visuals analyzed up to 100 pages)
Create files Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF; Create and edit files must be on
Artifacts Reusable, editable, shareable content
Projects Standing instructions and knowledge
Skills Repeatable procedures loaded when relevant
Images Reads images; does not generate photos
